The policy document is available as a PDF. [Download it](files/cb9-housing-analysis.pdf). The findings below are the ones the source tables support.

## Income differs inside the district

The 2023 five-year median in tract 219, in Manhattanville–West Harlem, is $20,912. The median in tract 205, in Morningside Heights, is $208,500. Those are medians of households of every size. They are not the share of residents who qualify for a unit, and they are not averaged into one district median. A three-person income limit and an all-household median describe different groups, so the analysis draws the limits as reference lines rather than as eligibility shares.

## The verified inventory is two buildings

HPD records PS 186 and Sunrose. Together they are 317 total units and 151 counted affordable units. HPD's income categories are not restated as a share at or below 60 percent of AMI. 1727 Amsterdam remains a proposal of about 200 units and stays out of the total. General Grant Houses, Morningside Gardens, ANCP, the Columbia Manhattanville project at 125 Amsterdam Avenue, 2975 Broadway, and Harlem Commons do not have a matching HPD row, so they are not added in.

## Service density is defined, and not scored

The saturation index compares mental-health sites, supportive units, and food pantries per 1,000 residents with the district average. The weighted formula is the definition. Without a facility list, the index has no score and no tract is placed in a policy band.

## Fair Share

In audit MD22-101A, BTP means beds-to-population. The audit's scope is fiscal years 2018 through 2022. It finds that most of the sitings it reviewed were not independently reviewed, and that a substantial share of the Article 9 sitings were in high beds-to-population districts, including districts in Manhattan. Community District 9 is among the districts the audit discusses.
